# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the

cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the

Arithmetic, deterministic, not stochastic:

   (`CG_RAIL_CORNER_OVERSHOOT`, a deliberate signed device that keeps arc credit ≤ displacement).
   At `CG_ROUTE_LONG` vertex 1 `(-26, 51.05, 14)` the published goal is `(-26, 51.05, 14.6)`,
   `arriveRadius = CG_RAIL_ROUTE_ARRIVE = 0.35`. Matches the captured rail exactly.
2. `agentSurfaceNavigation.worldToGrid` quantizes with `Math.round(w / VOXEL_SCALE)`, `VOXEL_SCALE = 2`.
   `round(14.6/2) = 7` → the goal's own cell centre is world `z = 14`. Every A* waypoint, including
   the last, is `voxelCoordToWorld(cell.support)` — a **snapped cell centre**, never the exact goal.
3. `primitives.nextNavigationStep`'s consumption loop stops at `waypoints.length - 1`, so the
   terminal snapped centre stays authoritative.
4. `primitives.steerFreeToward` clears all four controls inside tangent radius 0.2 (`lengthSq < 0.04`).
5. `walkToward` arrives only when `gaitDistance(exact goal) <= stop`.

Closest approach to the goal while steering is still active = `0.6 − 0.2 = 0.4 > 0.35`.
**The arrival predicate is analytically unsatisfiable.** The body parks inside the deadzone of the
cell centre, the rail keeps publishing `action=walk`, forever.

Verifier measurement fits: frozen tangent distance to `(-26,14)` = 0.1485 (run-1: 0.1706), to the
signed goal 0.7307, `arriveRadius` 0.35, `holdReason` null, `supported` true, displacement exactly 0.

`stillTime = 0` during a bit-identical frozen body is fully explained by
`primitives.ts:2138/2147`: `pushing = forward||backward||left||right`, and `stillTime` only
accumulates `if (pushing && delta < 0.06)`. The navigator is not pushing **at all**, so the watchdog
is correctly disarmed. It is not measuring the wrong body. No timeout teleport/nudge will be enabled.

This is NOT collision, water, hole, rise/drop, cross-face or unreachable goal: the planner resolved
the goal's OWN cell (`reason: dry-surface-path`), and the discriminator moved the real body freely.
It recurs at every subsequent corner (cursor 4 `x −30.6`, cursor 8 `z 22.6`, cursor 13 `x −42.6` —
each ≈0.75 short) because every one of those goals is the same ±0.6 overshoot past an even vertex.

  after the first director ticks. A pristine snapshot minted during boot permanently shadows the
  earned payload staged a moment later.
- **B — destructive autosave.** `persistence.saveWorld` writes a whole new `WorldSave`; the
  `commonGround` field is `serializeCommonGroundForWorld(worldId) ?? undefined`. A pristine live
  snapshot serializes to empty and replaces the earned blob; `null` would *delete* it instead.

"""Counterfactual: do the new tests actually fail on the PRE-REPAIR bytes?

Task-private, byte-exact, try/finally, hash-asserted on both ends. Never touches
Git. Run AFTER the repair edits existed; it swaps the four repaired sources for
their immutable before-bytes, runs the new/updated suites, and restores.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path("/home/thomasphillip/Projects/vox")
RUN = REPO / ".codex/production-runs/2026-09-05-after-the-hearth"
BEFORE = RUN / "iterations/implemented-world-repair/source"

TARGETS = [
    "main/src/story/autopilot/primitives.ts",
    "main/src/story/commonGroundState.ts",
    "main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.ts",
    "main/src/game/systems/persistence.ts",
]
SUITES = [
    "src/story/autopilot/primitives.test.ts",
    "src/story/commonGroundDirector.test.ts",
    "src/game/systems/persistence.test.ts",
]


def sha(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def main() -> int:
    backup_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="nav-counterfactual-", dir=str(RUN / "tmp")))
    repaired = {}
    original_before = {}
    try:
        for rel in TARGETS:
            live = REPO / rel
            before = BEFORE / rel
            if not before.exists():
                raise SystemExit(f"missing before-bytes for {rel}")
            repaired[rel] = sha(live)
            original_before[rel] = sha(before)
            dest = backup_dir / rel
            dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copy2(live, dest)
            assert sha(dest) == repaired[rel], f"backup mismatch {rel}"

        # --- swap in the pre-repair bytes ---------------------------------
        for rel in TARGETS:
            shutil.copy2(BEFORE / rel, REPO / rel)
            assert sha(REPO / rel) == original_before[rel], f"swap mismatch {rel}"

        result = subprocess.run(
            ["npx", "vitest", "run", *SUITES],
            cwd=str(REPO / "main"),
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=900,
        )
        tail = (result.stdout + result.stderr)[-6000:]
        (RUN / "tmp/navigation-counterfactual-output.txt").write_text(tail)
        print("PRE-REPAIR exit code:", result.returncode)
        for line in tail.splitlines():
            if "Tests " in line or "Test Files" in line or line.strip().startswith("×"):
                print(" ", line.strip())
        outcome = {
            "preRepairExitCode": result.returncode,
            "preRepairFailedAsExpected": result.returncode != 0,
        }
    finally:
        # --- restore, and PROVE the restore ------------------------------
        restored_ok = True
        for rel in TARGETS:
            src = backup_dir / rel
            if not src.exists():
                restored_ok = False
                continue
            shutil.copy2(src, REPO / rel)
            if sha(REPO / rel) != repaired[rel]:
                restored_ok = False
                print(f"RESTORE FAILED for {rel}", file=sys.stderr)
        print("restoreVerified:", restored_ok)
        # Immutable before-source must be untouched by this script.
        for rel in TARGETS:
            assert sha(BEFORE / rel) == original_before[rel], f"before-source mutated: {rel}"
        (RUN / "tmp/navigation-counterfactual-result.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    **(outcome if "outcome" in dir() else {}),
                    "restoreVerified": restored_ok,
                    "repairedSha256": repaired,
                    "beforeSha256": original_before,
                    "backupDir": str(backup_dir),
                },
                indent=1,
            )
        )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""NAV-RUNTIME-SEAM counterfactual.

Runs the real `autopilotTick` -> ch13 rail -> `walkToward` -> `nextNavigationStep`
-> `steerFreeToward` wiring against BOTH byte sets. The spec uses only exports
that exist on both, so a difference is behaviour, not API surface.

Root asked that temporary work reuse an existing ALLOWED test file rather than
introduce an unrouted path, so the spec is written into
main/src/story/autopilot/primitives.test.ts (already allowed) for the duration
of the run, with byte-exact backup and hash-verified restore in finally.
Never touches Git.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path("/home/thomasphillip/Projects/vox")
RUN = REPO / ".codex/production-runs/2026-09-05-after-the-hearth"
BEFORE = RUN / "iterations/implemented-world-repair/source"

SOURCES = ["main/src/story/autopilot/primitives.ts"]
SPEC_REL = "main/src/story/autopilot/primitives.test.ts"
SPEC_BODY = (RUN / "tmp/runtime-seam-spec.ts").read_text()


def sha(p: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def run(label: str) -> dict:
    r = subprocess.run(
        ["npx", "vitest", "run", "src/story/autopilot/primitives.test.ts"],
        cwd=str(REPO / "main"), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900,
    )
    blob = r.stdout + r.stderr
    (RUN / f"tmp/runtime-seam-{label}.txt").write_text(blob[-8000:])
    summary = next((l.strip() for l in blob.splitlines() if "Tests " in l), "?")
    print(f"[{label}] exit={r.returncode} :: {summary}")
    return {"label": label, "exitCode": r.returncode, "summary": summary}


def main() -> int:
    backup = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="runtime-seam-", dir=str(RUN / "tmp")))
    tracked = SOURCES + [SPEC_REL]
    original, before_sha = {}, {}
    findings = []
    try:
        for rel in tracked:
            original[rel] = sha(REPO / rel)
            dest = backup / rel
            dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copy2(REPO / rel, dest)
            assert sha(dest) == original[rel]
        for rel in SOURCES:
            before_sha[rel] = sha(BEFORE / rel)

        (REPO / SPEC_REL).write_text(SPEC_BODY)
        findings.append(run("repaired"))

        for rel in SOURCES:
            shutil.copy2(BEFORE / rel, REPO / rel)
            assert sha(REPO / rel) == before_sha[rel]
        findings.append(run("pre-repair"))
    finally:
        ok = True
        for rel in tracked:
            shutil.copy2(backup / rel, REPO / rel)
            if sha(REPO / rel) != original[rel]:
                ok = False
                print(f"RESTORE FAILED {rel}")
        for rel in SOURCES:
            assert sha(BEFORE / rel) == before_sha[rel], f"before-source mutated: {rel}"
        print("restoreVerified:", ok)
        (RUN / "tmp/runtime-seam-result.json").write_text(json.dumps({
            "findings": findings,
            "restoreVerified": ok,
            "restoredSha256": original,
            "beforeSha256": before_sha,
        }, indent=1))

"""NAV-RUNTIME-SEAM counterfactual.

Runs the real `autopilotTick` -> ch13 rail -> `walkToward` -> `nextNavigationStep`
-> `steerFreeToward` wiring against BOTH byte sets. The spec uses only exports
that exist on both, so a difference is behaviour, not API surface.

Root asked that temporary work reuse an existing ALLOWED test file rather than
introduce an unrouted path, so the spec is written into
main/src/story/autopilot/primitives.test.ts (already allowed) for the duration
of the run, with byte-exact backup and hash-verified restore in finally.
Never touches Git.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path("/home/thomasphillip/Projects/vox")
RUN = REPO / ".codex/production-runs/2026-09-05-after-the-hearth"
BEFORE = RUN / "iterations/implemented-world-repair/source"

SOURCES = ["main/src/story/autopilot/primitives.ts"]
SPEC_REL = "main/src/story/autopilot/primitives.test.ts"
SPEC_BODY = (RUN / "tmp/runtime-seam-spec.ts").read_text()


def sha(p: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def run(label: str) -> dict:
    r = subprocess.run(
        ["npx", "vitest", "run", "src/story/autopilot/primitives.test.ts"],
        cwd=str(REPO / "main"), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900,
    )
    blob = r.stdout + r.stderr
    (RUN / f"tmp/runtime-seam-{label}.txt").write_text(blob[-8000:])
    summary = next((l.strip() for l in blob.splitlines() if "Tests " in l), "?")
    print(f"[{label}] exit={r.returncode} :: {summary}")
    return {"label": label, "exitCode": r.returncode, "summary": summary}


def main() -> int:
    backup = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="runtime-seam-", dir=str(RUN / "tmp")))
    tracked = SOURCES + [SPEC_REL]
    original, before_sha = {}, {}
    findings = []
    try:
        for rel in tracked:
            original[rel] = sha(REPO / rel)
            dest = backup / rel
            dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copy2(REPO / rel, dest)
            assert sha(dest) == original[rel]
        for rel in SOURCES:
            before_sha[rel] = sha(BEFORE / rel)

        (REPO / SPEC_REL).write_text(SPEC_BODY)
        findings.append(run("repaired"))

        for rel in SOURCES:
            shutil.copy2(BEFORE / rel, REPO / rel)
            assert sha(REPO / rel) == before_sha[rel]
        findings.append(run("pre-repair"))
    finally:
        ok = True
        for rel in tracked:
            shutil.copy2(backup / rel, REPO / rel)
            if sha(REPO / rel) != original[rel]:
                ok = False
                print(f"RESTORE FAILED {rel}")
        for rel in SOURCES:
            assert sha(BEFORE / rel) == before_sha[rel], f"before-source mutated: {rel}"
        print("restoreVerified:", ok)
        (RUN / "tmp/runtime-seam-result.json").write_text(json.dumps({
            "findings": findings,
            "restoreVerified": ok,
            "restoredSha256": original,
            "beforeSha256": before_sha,
        }, indent=1))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Integration — navigation / Continue repair report

Run `2026-09-05-after-the-hearth` · integration-engineer · written **2026-09-06T13:47:05+00:00**
Direction `navigation-repair-direction.json` · defects **CG-IMPL-010 / 011 / 008**
Contract scene-v2 `4dbf722b…dff88e` — **unchanged**. No creative decision was made here.

**Not acceptance. Not chapter verification. No publication.**

---

## 1. What was wrong

### CG-IMPL-010 — VF4-SURVEY-STALL-1 (navigation)

The stall is **arithmetic, deterministic and unsatisfiable** — not a collision, not ground, not luck.

1. Chapter 13 aims `CG_RAIL_CORNER_OVERSHOOT` **0.6 through** each route corner — a signed device that
   keeps arc credit at or under real displacement. At `CG_ROUTE_LONG[1]` `(-26, 51.05, 14)` the published
   goal is `(-26, 51.05, 14.6)` with `arriveRadius` **0.35**. Exactly the captured rail.
2. `worldToGrid` quantizes `Math.round(w / VOXEL_SCALE)` with `VOXEL_SCALE = 2`, so `14.6` and `14.0`
   are the **same cell**. Every A* waypoint, including the terminal one, is
   `voxelCoordToWorld(cell.support)` — a **snapped cell centre**, never the exact goal.
3. `nextNavigationStep`'s consumption loop stops at `waypoints.length - 1`, so that centre stays the
   steering target forever.
4. `steerFreeToward` releases **all four controls** within tangent radius **0.2** of it.
5. `walkToward` arrives only on the distance to the goal the caller actually asked for.

> Closest possible approach while steering is live: **0.6 − 0.2 = 0.4 > 0.35**.

The body parks, the rail keeps publishing `action: walk`, forever. It recurs at *every* later corner
(cursor 4 `x −30.6`, cursor 8 `z 22.6`, cursor 13 `x −42.6`, each ≈0.75 short) because each is the same
±0.6 overshoot past an even vertex — which is why one nudge could never repair the remaining route.

**`stillTime = 0` beside a bit-identical body is fully explained.** The stuck watchdog accumulates only
`if (pushing && horizontalDelta < 0.06)`, and `pushing` is the OR of the four controls. The navigator
issues *nothing*, so `pushing` is false and the timer resets every frame. It is not measuring the wrong
body — it is correctly disarmed. **No timeout teleport, nudge or rescue escalation was enabled.**

### CG-IMPL-011 / 008 — the Continue loss

Two coupled defects, isolated by ordering rather than inferred from the storage snapshot:

- **Restore shadowing.** `commonGroundSnapshot` returned a cached live snapshot *before* consulting the
  staged payload. `restoreCommonGroundForWorld` is a world-keyed React effect, so an empty placeholder
  minted by an earlier read permanently shadowed the earned bytes staged a moment later.
- **Destructive autosave.** `saveWorld` writes a whole new record; `commonGround` was
  `serializeCommonGroundForWorld(worldId) ?? undefined`. A placeholder overwrote the earned blob with
  emptiness (1186 → 606 bytes, 4 samples → 0); a `null` would have deleted it outright.

The write is **not** attributed to clicking Continue: boot, the placeholder-minting *read*, the world
switch and the world-change autosave are stepped separately, and the read is named as the culprit frame.

**`PC-CONTINUE-RESUME-POINT` is a fixture predecessor gap, not a wrong-world-selection bug.** The deep
link seeded `ch13-fault-reviewed` + `ch13-return-chosen` but never `story:ch13-origin-landed`, and
`storyEntryPoint` resolves precisely that set to `ch13-return`. Proved both ways: without the milestone
the entry is `ch13-return`; with it, `ch13-survey`, and the same saved bytes resume the drawing.

---

## 2. The repair

**Navigation** — `terminalExactGoalHandoff` + `applyTerminalExactGoal`. At the terminal waypoint *only*,
the exact goal takes over the last leg when **all** hold: the planner resolved the goal's own cell
(`dry-surface-path` / `already-at-resolved-goal`, not wet, not substituted); same face, no cross-face leg;
not a water/jetpack leg; the goal lies inside the terminal cell's tangential footprint; and every further
column the capsule actually overlaps is certified **by the same planner at the same surface height**. The
aim then moves *tangentially only*, at the height the planner cleared, and the body walks the rest under
ordinary directional input.

Two asymmetries, both matching the planner's own contract: only the **tangent** axes are compared
(`worldToGrid` projects onto `tangentU`/`tangentV`; the normal index is not cell identity, and foot goal
51.05 / grounded 50.989 / waypoint 52.85 are three legitimate conventions for one place), and the
footprint is **certified against real terrain** rather than capped by an arbitrary offset limit, so a
signed 0.6 overshoot stays reachable wherever the ground is genuinely safe.

Not done: arrival radius unchanged · dead zone value unchanged (only *named*, so the arithmetic is
testable) · no authored pose/route/proof touched · no corner credit increased · no distance paid by
endpoint motion · no clamp, teleport or grant · no rescue · navigator not bypassed.

**Shared-walker compatibility, proved rather than asserted:** before, arrival needed
`stop ≥ 0.2 + |goal − centre|`; after, only `stop ≥ 0.2`. The second is implied by the first for every
offset, so **no goal that used to be reached can stop being reached**. The smallest stop radius in any
shipped rail is 0.3. Terrain, hazard, water and cross-face protection are untouched because the handoff
never leaves a certified cell and is refused outright on those cases.

**Continue** — `serializeCommonGroundForWorld` returns null when it cannot speak for a world; `saveWorld`
**carries the persisted blob forward** instead of dropping or replacing it; a staged payload may take over
an empty placeholder but **never real progress**; a world is *settled* only when its restore found
**nothing** (absent/legacy) or when a payload actually **validated** — a completed read of a present
payload settles nothing; and `clearCommonGroundForWorld` now removes the stored chapter field so
carry-forward cannot resurrect it.

---

## 3. Root's review items — all closed in source

| item | resolution |
| --- | --- |
| **NAV-HEIGHT** | `certifyColumn` returns the planner's *resolved surface*; the helper compares it against the terminal along `up` and refuses beyond half a cell (`footprint-height-mismatch`). Dry is not safe — a wall top and a pit floor are both dry. Proved with in-cube stepped terrain, raised and lowered both refused, flat control still allowed. |
| **NAV-RUNTIME-SEAM** | A test drives the real `autopilotTick → ch13 rail → walkToward → nextNavigationStep → steerFreeToward` in movie mode at the captured frozen pose, observing only shipped `getAutopilotControls()`. Same spec on pre-repair bytes: **`expected 0 to be greater than 0`** — no control on any of 30 frames. |
| **NAV-EXACT-CACHE** | Cached per *(plan, exact goal)*; the route cache tolerates ~1 unit of drift, so a stale certification can no longer authorise a moved target. Probes re-run only on real target change; no full A* forced. Focused same-plan test: two sub-unit-apart targets, two different lawful answers. |
| **SAVE-ENTRY-BEFORE-RESTORE** | The first `entered` candidate was **withdrawn** — beat entry as ownership would have made the placeholder authoritative and reinstated the bug. Ownership is now driven only by persistence. Covered: entry before staging, restore that finds nothing, and a new action after a bare entry. |
| **SAVE-SCOPED-CLEAR** | Clears live/pending maps **and** the stored chapter field only; structures, campfires, habitat and other worlds untouched. clear → save → reload does not resurrect it. |
| **SAVE-ENTRY staging window** (13:41) | A completed read of a *present* payload no longer settles. An autosave landing between staging and hydration keeps the earned bytes, which then hydrate on the next tick. |
| **SAVE-ENTRY foreign payload** (13:41) | Now rewrites the **actual stored record** and goes through the real restore route. A rejected payload deliberately does not settle, so local empty state can never overwrite it. |

---

## 4. Changed paths (exact SHA)

| path | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main/src/story/autopilot/primitives.ts` | `4cce7261…13ca` | `a6da0551…a4ae` |
| `main/src/story/autopilot/primitives.test.ts` | **null** (demonstrably absent) | `158f5ac9…2f2d` |
| `main/src/story/commonGroundState.ts` | `2094b261…db2bf` | `681846b7…87a6` |
| `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.ts` | `5688b86e…4d6b3` | `23bd8ea5…921f` |
| `main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.test.ts` | `58bc30b4…3008` | `8584dc5c…87ac` |
| `main/src/game/systems/persistence.ts` | `c8d51b1d…5404` | `f68be69f…631d` |
| `main/src/game/systems/persistence.test.ts` | `c0c2b159…d734` | `9c1dd65d…517a` |

All seven are inside `production-lock.allowedPaths`. **6 of the 97 manifest files changed; unexpected
drift on the other 91: none.** 323 pre-existing dirty files preserved. No protected, shared or global
workflow file touched. **`git checkout/reset/restore/stash/clean` was never invoked.**

---

## 5. Checks

| command | cwd | exit | result | log sha256 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run verify` | `/home/thomasphillip/Projects/vox/main` | **0** | 350 files / **3137** tests | `e6f6afdb…daa5` |
| `npm run story:ux:check` | same | **0** | 9 files / 94 tests | `77c95c2b…7a45` |

`verify` covers catalog, scene-AV, creative-workflow, chapter registry, chapter journey, typecheck,
preview, audio diagnostic, story ladder, guidance targets, story authority, tests, audio, build.

**+46 added, 0 removed, 2 changed.** Added: primitives 29, director 11, persistence 6.

the world's restore in its first session too (the runtime always does; the test omitted it), and the
foreign-actor case now goes through the real on-disk route instead of a hand-staged copy. Every original
assertion in both is retained.

| probe | pre-repair | repaired | restore |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tmp/continue-counterfactual.py` | `phase=idle samples=0 bytes=563` | `phase=drawing samples=4 bytes=909` | verified |

`primitives.test.ts` with byte-exact backup and hash-verified restore.

  branch; explicit clear reclaims the record.

steering intent and dead zone, the *real* arrival measure, the *real* `autopilotTick` control output, and

content.text:
Bounded repair complete. Source is frozen for root review.

## What was wrong

**CG-IMPL-010 (VF4-SURVEY-STALL-1)** was arithmetic, not chance. Chapter 13 aims 0.6 *through* each route corner; with `VOXEL_SCALE = 2` that goal quantizes into the **same cell** as the vertex, and every A* waypoint — including the terminal one, which is never consumed — is a snapped **cell centre**. `steerFreeToward` drops all four controls within 0.2 of that centre, while `walkToward` arrives only on distance to the real goal. Closest possible approach: **0.6 − 0.2 = 0.4 > 0.35**. The arrival predicate was *unsatisfiable*. It recurs at every later corner, which is why one nudge never fixed the route.

`stillTime = 0` beside a frozen body is fully explained: the watchdog counts only while `pushing`, and the navigator was issuing nothing. Correctly disarmed — I did not arm it.

**CG-IMPL-011/008**: an empty placeholder snapshot, minted by a read before the world-keyed restore effect ran, both shadowed the earned payload and got serialized over it (1186 → 606 bytes, 4 samples → 0). I isolated the *frame*, rather than blaming the Continue click.

## Two judgement calls worth flagging

**The resume point is not a bug.** The fixture seeded `fault-reviewed` + `return-chosen` but never `ch13-origin-landed`, and `storyEntryPoint` resolves exactly that set to `ch13-return`. I proved it both ways rather than "fixing" lawful behaviour.

**I withdrew my own first Continue candidate.** Root pointed out that treating beat entry as world ownership would make the very placeholder authoritative and reinstate the bug. That was correct — ownership is now driven only by persistence, and only a restore that found *nothing* or a payload that *validated* settles a world.

## The proof that matters

The helper tests alone weren't sufficient, so there is now a test driving the real `autopilotTick → ch13 rail → walkToward → nextNavigationStep → steerFreeToward`, observing only shipped controls. Run against pre-repair bytes: **`expected 0 to be greater than 0`** — no movement asked for on any of 30 frames. The Continue counterfactual reads `phase=idle samples=0` before, `phase=drawing samples=4` after.

`npm run verify` exit **0**, 350 files / **3137** tests (+46, −0, 2 made lifecycle-faithful without dropping an assertion). 6 of 97 manifest files changed, **zero unexpected drift**, 323 dirty files preserved, no destructive Git.

## Honest limitations

- One counterfactual briefly created a file **outside allowedPaths**; it didn't pre-exist, removal is proven, and later work reused an allowed file as root asked. Recorded rather than buried.
- Reproductions ran **after** edits began — not claimed otherwise. An early draft used the grounded frame instead of the capsule centre the navigator reads, and failed for the wrong reason until corrected.
- **HABITAT-CARRY-SYMMETRY**: `saveWorld`'s `habitat` field has the same drop-shaped defect the `commonGround` field had. Not demonstrated by any capture and out of scope, so I flagged it for routing rather than silently widening.
- **Nothing here is a hardware claim.** VF4 was found on GB10 and must be re-measured there; preview 40131 is pre-repair source and cannot validate this.
